subject: Dedicated reservation options: cluster sizes, min GPUs, and ramp schedule
messages:
From: Lucas Reed <lucas.reed@sierrahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity options for pilot -> committed deployment

Logan —

Thanks for the quick chat this morning. We scoped an internal brief and want to see a short set of reserved capacity options tied to our pilot-to-prod ramp. High level asks:
- Three commitment profiles (conservative, mid, aggressive) with cluster size (total GPUs), minimum guaranteed GPUs, and suggested ramp schedule over 6 months.
- Cost deltas and estimated per-token unit cost changes between profiles.
- Warm-start / pre-warm recommendations and any activation credits for initial months.

Can you send something we can present to our procurement folks next week? Also include any SLA differences if we need hard latency targets for certain inference routes.

— Lucas
CTO, SierraHealth
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Reed <lucas.reed@sierrahealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-10T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options for pilot -> committed deployment

Lucas —

Thanks — attached is a concise options pack (sierra_dedicated_options_v1.pdf) and an activation timeline spreadsheet. Summary in short:

1) Conservative profile (Pilot-first)
- Cluster: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Min guaranteed: 4 GPUs (soft floor)
- Ramp: 0-2 months: pilot on shared burst; 3-6 months: step to guaranteed 4 GPUs -> optional surge for peak hours
- Cost: baseline monthly commit $55k; expected marginal token cost +18% vs hosted.

2) Mid profile (Steady growth)
- Cluster: 24x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Min guaranteed: 12 GPUs (hard floor)
- Ramp: month 1-2 get 6 GPUs online; month 3 activate 12; month 5-6 scale toward 24 as usage converts
- Cost: monthly commit $150k; marginal token cost +8% vs hosted; includes 1 month activation credit equal to $15k.

3) Aggressive profile (Production at scale)
- Cluster: 64x A100-equivalent GPUs (multi-pod)
- Min guaranteed: 32 GPUs (hard floor)
- Ramp: phased across 6 months with staged activation windows and automated warm pools
- Cost: monthly commit $360k; marginal token cost -2% vs hosted at steady state; includes 2 months activation credit + a one-time warm-start assistance package.

SLA notes: hard-floor profiles (mid/aggressive) qualify for 99.95% uptime and latency SLOs we can contract per-route. Conservative soft-floor has best-effort latency SLOs with fallbacks to hosted.

Next steps: if you can flag which profile the procurement team prefers, we’ll provide a final quote and a suggested paperwork cadence (deal desk -> legal -> Po execution).

Attaching activation_timeline_sheet.xlsx with the step-up calendar and suggested health checks during each activation window.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity options for SierraHealth — need pricing granularity and activation runbook

Team —

Looping you in. Lucas (SierraHealth CTO) asked for three commitment profiles; I put a short summary in the attached PDF. Ask: can you 1) confirm the monthly commit numbers I put are within allowable discount bands for a first-year contract and 2) add a brief activation runbook we can include (ideal lead times, pre-warm steps, test traffic gating) and call out any potential resource constraints for a 6-month ramp to 64 GPUs?

Ben — pricing and credits.
Karthik — operations/activation runbook.

Quick replies OK — procurement meeting on 06/15.

— Logan

On Jun 11, 2026, karthik.iyer@redwood.com wrote: 
> Logan —
>
> For a 6-month phased ramp to 64 GPUs, main risks are inventory cadence (availability of A100-equivalent slots) and warm-cache ramping for high-QPS routes. Recommended runbook:
> - Week 0-2: baseline capacity reservation + staging lane; deploy smoke tests
> - Week 3-6: enable prefix caching and KV cache prefill for targeted models; run load-tests at 30% production QPS
> - Month 2-4: scale guaranteed GPUs to 50% target; enable autoscaling triggers for peak windows
> - Month 5-6: full activation with multi-pod routing and redundancy
>
> I can produce a 1-page runbook snippet for the doc.
>
> — Karthik
From: Lucas Reed <lucas.reed@sierrahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: SierraHealth Procurement <procurement@sierrahealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options for pilot -> committed deployment

Logan —

This is helpful, thanks. Procurement asked for two clarifications before the 06/15 meeting:
1) For the mid profile: can you show a simple comparison of costs if we front-load ramp (activate 12 GPUs month 1) vs your suggested gradual ramp? We need to know breakeven timing against hosted pricing.
2) For the SLA: what happens to latency-sensitive routes if we hit the soft floor on the conservative profile? Is there an automated fallback to hosted that preserves latency but increases unit cost?

We’re leaning toward the mid profile but may propose the front-loaded variant if the math favors fewer months-to-break-even. Also please put the activation runbook onto Redwood letterhead for procurement.

— Lucas
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Reed <lucas.reed@sierrahealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, SierraHealth Procurement <procurement@sierrahealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options — follow-ups and next steps

Lucas —

Great questions. Short answers:
1) Front-loaded mid profile: we ran the numbers. If you activate 12 GPUs in month 1 (vs step to 6 then to 12), breakeven against hosted pricing moves ~1.8 months earlier because steady-state unit cost applies sooner. I attached an extra tab in the spreadsheet with a front-loaded vs staged cost curve.
2) Conservative soft-floor fallback: yes — Redwood can route latency-sensitive routes to hosted variants automatically when the soft floor is saturated. That preserves latency SLOs but will materialize at the hosted unit cost; the routing is per-route and configurable as part of the rollout policy. We’ll document default fallback behavior and the opt-in gating for procurement.

Action items:
- Ben: finalize a commercial quote with two mid-profile variants (staged vs front-loaded) and include activation credits line items.
- Karthik: convert your runbook into a 1-page activation appendix on Redwood letterhead (PDF).
- Logan: deliver final package (quote + appendix + contract cadence) by EOD 06/14 so SierraHealth procurement can review before the meeting on 06/15.

If that timeline is tight on your side, call and I’ll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
